clue.text: Nice to see gold suit put back in fancy blue wrapping

indicators.note: the scrambled blue is wrapped around the gold and suit pieces, enclosing them
fancy here means elaborately reworked, so the letters of blue are rearranged

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: put back means the word for suit is written in reverse order

parts.note: to suit is to fit, as clothes do

explanation.surface: A shopper admires a gold outfit wrapped in elegant blue paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice to see' is a phrase meaning lovely to look at, not a greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lovely is pleasing to look at, a phrase-level synonym for attractive.

clue.text: Only 100mph for a fast driver?

parts.note: only, as in 'only that', can mean but
a ton is slang for a hundred miles an hour

explanation.surface: A sneer at a racing driver who manages a mere hundred miles an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenson Button is a British Formula One world champion; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Jenson Button raced in Formula One, so he is an example of a speedy racer behind the wheel.

clue.text: A rising revolutionary in Aquarius say?

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns things over, so the letters of 'A rising' are rearranged

explanation.surface: An uprising led by a radical born under Aquarius.
explanation.definitionFit: In astrology Aquarius is one of the three zodiac signs of the air element, so it is an example.

clue.text: Short of ecstasy, erotic magic could be seriously funny

indicators.note: could be signals the remaining letters may be arranged into something else
short of means lacking, so one letter is dropped from the fodder

parts.note: E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A stage magician's racy act without drugs might be hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of' drops an E from EROTIC MAGIC, leaving ROTICMAGIC, which 'could be' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragicomic drama mixes the grave and the comic, so it is funny in a serious way.

clue.text: List of plants fellow read occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: A man reads now and then from a catalogue of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: The flora of a region is the plants found there, and a book cataloguing them bears the same name.

clue.text: Dollars spread around North Dakota in letters

indicators.note: around means the scrambled dollars lie on both sides of the state abbreviation
spread means scattered, so the letters of dollars are rearranged

parts.note: ND is the postal abbreviation for the US state of North Dakota

explanation.surface: Money scattered across a US state, recorded in correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' looks like correspondence but means people who let out property.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who let houses or rooms to tenants are property owners collecting rent.

clue.text: A painter's become deflated?

definitions.meaning: Edgar ... was a French Impressionist artist
read as ..., to lose one's gas, like a punctured balloon

explanation.surface: An artist has lost his puff.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist known for ballet dancers; split, the name reads as losing gas.

clue.text: A stately building to meet my requirements?

definitions.meaning: a grand rounded-roof structure such as a cathedral or the Millennium edifice
read as ..., to suit or serve me

explanation.surface: A grand building that is just what I need.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupola-topped hall is an imposing structure; split in two the word says 'serve me'.

clue.text: When at sea, get bang out of this?

definitions.text: When at sea, get bang out of this?

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of bang out are rearranged

explanation.surface: A naval vessel fires loud shots once it is out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a small armed warship at sea is where bangs come from.
explanation.definitionFit: An armed naval vessel firing its cannon produces bangs, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Make The Sound Of Music around mountain top — not while doing this

indicators.note: around means the singing word is placed on both sides of the summit word

parts.note: to make music with the voice is to sing; the capitals point at the film
a peak is the top of a mountain

explanation.surface: A Julie Andrews film scene: singing on a mountain top, with no chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: One cannot sing while talking, so 'not while doing this' points back to the singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Talking is the activity one cannot do while singing, so the phrase describes it obliquely.

clue.text: Rent trouble? This is quite a blow

parts.note: rent, the past tense of rend, means torn
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A tenant laments a rent dispute as a real blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord but means ripped.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a violent whirlwind, so it is a very strong blow of wind.

clue.text: I'm named Head of Explosives after results of bomb disposal

indicators.note: after places the explosives letter at the end, following the other piece

parts.note: once a bomb is disposed of there is NO MINE left

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of explosives is taken

explanation.surface: A bomb-squad officer is appointed head of explosives after successful clearances.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate put forward for a post has been named, so can say of themself they are the one chosen.

clue.text: Friend axes meeting place making a switch first

indicators.note: the switch swaps the order, so the second piece in the clue comes first

parts.note: on a graph the x and y axes meet at the origin
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend chops at a meeting venue, changing things round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' looks like a verb of chopping but is the plural of axis.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean at the start, as in 'at first' or 'in the beginning'.

clue.text: Swing as a musical genre?

definitions.meaning: to swing is to sway back and forth
a popular music style, as in the roll partner

explanation.surface: Is swing a kind of music?
explanation.walkthrough: Swing is itself a jazz style, so the surface tempts a single definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To sway to and fro is to move like a cradle; the word also names a loud guitar-based music style.

clue.text: Advisers advanced to repair American city resorts for some Londoners

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
to repair to a place is to go there
NY is New York
haunts, said by a Cockney who drops the H

explanation.surface: Consultants hurry to fix favourite spots in an American city for Londoners.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class East Londoners, famously drop the initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Magazine columnists answering readers' personal problems are counsellors offering guidance.

clue.text: Medical specialism with not one medic to dispose of the dead

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat medicine
not one is none, zero, the letter O
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A hospital department lacking doctors deals with corpses.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury a body in a tomb is a way of laying the deceased to rest.

clue.text: A lover of ornate finery in a person's embrace

indicators.note: the person's embrace holds the scrambled letters inside

parts.note: a bod is informal for a person

indicators.note: ornate means elaborately worked, so the letters of finery are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dandy who loves fine clothes is held in someone's arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A male partner in a romantic relationship is someone's sweetheart.

clue.text: Trendy town but not the capital

indicators.note: the capital here is the initial capital letter, which is removed

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside town on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A fashionable place that is not London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a capital city but means the town's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fashionable and up to date in attitude is slang for being correct and current.

clue.text: Bordered by a lot of flags, central section of mullioned building

indicators.note: bordered by means the paving word sits around the middle of the window word
a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter of the flags word goes

parts.note: flagstones laid together make paving

indicators.note: central section means only the middle three letters of mullioned are kept

explanation.surface: A mullioned building with flagstones laid all round it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flags' looks like banners but means paving stones.
explanation.definitionFit: A pavilion is a building, such as a cricket clubhouse or an ornamental summer house.

clue.text: Not even a hint of overdraft with direct debit

indicators.note: a hint of means only the opening letter of overdraft is used

parts.note: DD is the banking abbreviation for direct debit

explanation.surface: A bank statement shows a slight overdraft from an automatic payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even' looks like 'not even a hint', but 'Not even' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers not divisible by two are uneven, the opposite of even.

clue.text: Approve the thing next year as an asset to the community

parts.note: saying amen expresses approval
it means the thing

explanation.surface: A council approves a project for next year as good for the community.
explanation.definitionFit: A useful facility such as a park or library benefits the local people.

clue.text: Eastern variety of marled stone

indicators.note: variety of means a different form, so the letters of marled are rearranged

explanation.surface: An oriental type of streaky rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A green beryl is a precious gem, and gemstones are called stones.

clue.text: Assorted fine weather without rain

parts.note: sun is fine weather
dry means without rain

explanation.surface: A mixed forecast: fine and rainless.
explanation.definitionFit: Various or miscellaneous items are a mixed collection, as in 'all and sundry'.

clue.text: Tell composer endless passage needs a bit of imagination

indicators.note: endless means both outer letters are cut away

parts.note: a crossing is a passage, over a sea or road

indicators.note: a bit of means just the first letter of imagination

explanation.surface: Talk about a composer whose long piece needs some imagination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' looks like a verb but is the opera William Tell.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini wrote the opera William Tell, famous for its overture.

clue.text: Lively zebra with eye mostly for a run

indicators.note: colours that run blur and mix, so the letters are rearranged
for means one piece stands in place of another
mostly means the final letter of eye is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spirited zebra keeps an eye out while running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts EYE to EY, which replaces the A of ZEBRA ('for a'); 'run' then rearranges ZEBREY.
explanation.definitionFit: A breezy manner is cheerful and light-hearted, a synonym for sprightly.

clue.text: With added chilli, seeing special takeaway is not at all hot

indicators.note: takeaway means the letters for special are removed

parts.note: food with chilli added is spiced

explanation.surface: A spiced special from the takeaway turns out stone cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' looks like chilli heat but means temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilled or frozen is the opposite of warm, so cold food is far from hot.

clue.text: Misplaced individual, very unfashionable for a Parisian run

parts.note: in French tres means very and passe means outmoded
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A lost soul, hopelessly out of style, goes jogging in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder is somewhere they should not be, so is a person out of place.

clue.text: To play guitar on the street is unusual?

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Is busking with a guitar out of doors odd?
explanation.definitionFit: Brushing the fingers across guitar strings is a way of playing the instrument.

clue.text: Seaside attraction ripe for development

indicators.note: development means reshaping, so the letters of ripe are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coastal amusement is ready to be developed.
explanation.definitionFit: A jetty with amusements is a classic British seafront feature, like Brighton's.

clue.text: Conjure up how one of the spirits might introduce itself at end of séance?

parts.words: how one of the spirits might introduce itself
parts.note: a gin, one of the spirits, would say I'M A GIN

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of séance is taken

explanation.surface: A medium summons a ghost who announces itself as the séance closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' suggests ghosts at a séance but means strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something in the mind is to call it up mentally, to dream it.

clue.text: How long program lasts is finally under minute perhaps?

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of under
perhaps hints the letters of minute may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Does the software finish in under a minute?
explanation.definitionFit: The duration of a computer program's execution is its execution period.

clue.text: Lowest point of drain complex

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so the letters of drain are rearranged

explanation.surface: The bottom of a complicated drainage system.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom or worst moment is the low-water mark, opposite of zenith.

clue.text: Shed light on stand up to about my top of shelving and over it

indicators.note: about means the defiance word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to defy is to stand up to

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of shelving
over means the word it is turned backwards

explanation.surface: Puzzling over standing up to my shelving and climbing on top of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To clarify something is to make it less mysterious, to explain it.
